name: Parallel LFR-like Benchmark
description: Community detection is one of the most widely-used graph analytics. As recent community detection algorithms have been targeting large-scale networks, an emerging problem is how best to evaluate the output of these algorithms. Common measures such as modularity have several well-known issues, so comparisons against a notion of a “ground truth” community structure, such as in the Lancicinetti-Fortunato-Radicchi (LFR) benchmark, is preferred. This current work targets the parallel generation of graphs matching the specifications of the LFR benchmark. We are able to generate such graphs at the billion-edge scale in seconds, giving orders-of-magnitude speedup relative to prior work.
evaluation_method: Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) / Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)
reputation: A niche but useful synthetic benchmark for scalable community-detection evaluation—used in research on parallel graph generators and large-scale community detection.
notes: Synthetic LFR-like graphs with planted communities; non-LLM benchmark. Highly configurable for scale and noise but may not fully reflect real-world network properties; low contamination risk.
